outcome: No result changing the stated bounds or resolving any case of tripod packing was found published or announced between 26 January 2024 and today (22 September 2026).
summary: Tripod packing asks how many disjoint tripods (Stein's 'semicrosses'/'Stein corners') can have their apexes packed into an n×n×n grid. As of the current live Wikipedia article, the best lower bound is Ω(n^1.546) (Gowers and Long, 2021) and the best upper bound is n²/2^Ω(log* n), derived via the Ruzsa–Szemerédi problem — both established before the 26 January 2024 frozen revision date. I ran searches for a proof, disproof, new bound, or any case-settling result on tripod packing (also trying the historical names 'semicross' and 'Stein corners'), searches specifically for post-2024 arXiv papers, and searches for any AI-system involvement (e.g., DeepMind AlphaEvolve/FunSearch-style results, which have recently touched circle-packing and sphere-packing variants but not this problem). None turned up any post-January-2024 development on this problem's own bounds. The only 2024+ hits were irrelevant homonyms (camera/photography tripods, an unrelated deep-learning model named 'Tripod', unrelated packing papers on spheres, cylinders, and bin packing). I also checked the Wikipedia article's own edit/citation history via the live page (most recent citations are 2021 and 2019) and confirmed no newer citations appear. Note the triage record's stated lower bound, Ω(n^(2/3)), does not match the Ω(n^1.546) figure I found on both the live and (per the triage's own citation trail) presumably the frozen-era article; Ω(n^1.546) is the Gowers–Long 2021 result and is the figure that should be treated as the pre-2024 baseline. This appears to be a triage transcription/recall error rather than a substantive disagreement about post-2024 events, since no matter which baseline is used, no post-2024 movement was found either way.
competing_reading: It is conceivable a paper improving the bound exists in a venue not well indexed by general web search (e.g., a discrete geometry conference proceedings or a national mathematical society journal not on arXiv), given this is a fairly niche problem with a small community. I could not rule this out with certainty, though the problem's visibility (it has its own Wikipedia article and is referenced in surveys) makes it likely that any improvement would surface in general search results or in citations to the Gowers–Long paper.
what_would_settle_it: A citation search (e.g., via Semantic Scholar or Google Scholar, which were not directly queryable here beyond web search) specifically for papers citing Gowers & Long's 'On the density of tripod-packings' or Aronov et al.'s work, filtered to 2024 onward, would give the most authoritative confirmation that no citing improvement exists.
